message.description:

ApplyStatusOverrideRequest.description: Sets a manual status override on a service.

reason.description:
Required on purpose: an override hides the measured truth from everyone
reading the statuspage, so it always has to say why.

checked_at.description: When the check ran: ISO 8601, UTC, millisecond precision.

error_message.description: Why the check did not pass, as a short readable reason (e.g. `Connection refused`); null when there is nothing to report.

probe.description: The probe (monitoring location) that ran the check: a location code as listed by `GET /v1/probes`.

response_time_ms.description: How long the check took, in milliseconds.

status.description: The result of this one check: `up`, `down` or `degraded`.

status_code.description: The HTTP status code the target answered with; null for checks that are not HTTP and when no response arrived.

timings.description:

install_command.description: Run once on the server, as root. Installs the agent and enrolls it with this key.

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked (ISO 8601); null while it was not.

services.description:

tags.description: Every server enrolled with this key gets these tags; the server cannot replace them.

token_prefix.description:

response that created it.

type.description: `single` enrolls exactly one server, `fleet` up to `max_uses` servers.

verified_at.description: When the DNS records were verified (ISO 8601); null until then.

DeclareHeartbeatsRequest.description:
Declares the heartbeats an application expects in one environment. Send the whole list every
time: heartbeats that are new are created, heartbeats whose declaration changed are updated,
everything else is left alone. Nothing is ever deleted.

app.description:
The application the heartbeats belong to, e.g. `shop`. Lowercase letters, digits,
`.`, `_` and `-`; it starts and ends with a letter or digit. An organization can
declare heartbeats for up to 50 applications.

environment.description:
The environment the application runs in, e.g. `production`. Same characters as
`app`. A declaration only ever touches heartbeats of its own environment. An
organization can use up to 20 environments.

heartbeats.description:
Every heartbeat the application expects in this environment, at most 400. A
heartbeat declared earlier that is missing from the list is not touched; it is
named under `unlisted` in the response.

grace_seconds.description: Seconds a ping may be late before it counts as missed. 60 for a new heartbeat.

key.description:
What your code calls the heartbeat, e.g. `export:nightly`. Letters, digits, `.`,
`_`, `-`, `:` and `/`; it starts and ends with a letter or digit and is
case-sensitive. Together with `app` and `environment` it identifies the heartbeat,
so each key may appear once in the list.

kind.description: What the heartbeat watches: `schedule` (a scheduled task), `job`, `queue` or `custom`.

max_duration_seconds.description:
Longest time in seconds a run may take between its start ping and its end ping.
Send null to remove the limit; omit the field to leave it as it is.

name.description:
The name shown in LIVCK. Only used when the heartbeat is created (the key when
omitted); renaming it later never changes it back.

expression.description:
For `cron`: a cron expression with five fields (minute, hour, day of month, month,
day of week).

period_seconds.description:
For `simple`: seconds between two pings. A value below the shortest period of your
plan is raised to it; the response shows the value in effect.

timezone.description:
IANA time zone the cron expression is read in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. A new
heartbeat without one uses UTC.

type.description:
`simple`: a ping is expected every `period_seconds`. `cron`: a ping is expected
whenever `expression` is due.

schedule_tolerance.description:
How many expected pings in a row have to be missed before the heartbeat is down.
A new heartbeat gets 2 when it is expected at least every five minutes, else 1.

DeclareHeartbeatsRequest.title: DeclareHeartbeatsRequest

conditions.description: Status rules evaluated against each check result. The fields and operators valid for this check type are listed at GET /v1/meta/check-types.

changes.description:
Before and after per field, spelled like the rule fields (`nameservers`, `registrar`,
`statuses`, `lifecycle`, `expires_at`, `dnssec`, `in_zone`, `registration`). Empty for a
type this API version does not describe yet.

type.description:
What changed: `nameservers_changed`, `registrar_changed`, `statuses_changed`,
`lifecycle_changed`, `expiry_changed`, `dnssec_changed`, `zone_lost`, `zone_restored`,
`became_available` or `registered`. New types may be added.

reason.description: The notice as one sentence, in the language negotiated with `Accept-Language`.

rule.description: The rule key that fired, e.g. `nameservers_changed`, `expiry_14`, `transfer_lock`.

seen_at.description: When somebody marked it as seen in the console (ISO 8601); null while it is open.

alarm.description:
The open domain alarm (an incident of kind `domain`) with the rules that fired for this
domain; null when there is none.

baseline.description:
The expected state the rule operator `changed` compares the facts with, and where the
facts deviate from it (`before` = expected, `after` = now); null before the first check.

checked_at.description: When the domain's zone was last checked (ISO 8601); null before the first check.

domain.description: The registrable domain in ASCII, lower case (Punycode for an internationalized name).

facts.description:
The confirmed facts of the domain, as far as this watch may see them; null before its
first check. A fact that is not known is null.

first_observed_at.description: When this watch's first check was done (ISO 8601); null before it.

monitored_since.description: When the organization started watching the domain (ISO 8601).

next_check_at.description: When the next check is due (ISO 8601); null before the first check.

observed.description:
Whether this watch's own first check is done. Until then `facts`, `baseline` and
`alarm` are null.

sources.description: The services that watch this domain (only those this token may see).

state.description:
`pending` until the first check of this watch is done, then `ok`, `drift` (facts differ
from the baseline), `notice` (a notice rule fires) or `alarm` (an alarm rule fires).

unicode_domain.description: The same domain in Unicode; the same as `domain` for an ASCII name.

window_start.description:
The regular start of the running window (UTC, ISO 8601), as `window_start` of that
window in GET …/windows or GET /v1/maintenance-windows. It names the window you
mean: if another window is running by the time the request arrives, it is refused
with 409.

EnrollAgentRequest.description:
Register a server agent. Authenticate with an enrollment token (`lve_…`), or with the
agent's own token (`lvk_…`) to register it again. A malformed body is answered with 422 and
`{"error": {"code": "INVALID_REQUEST", "message": "…", "fields": {…}}}`; sending it again
unchanged will not succeed.

fingerprint.description: Identifying facts of the machine, up to 16 entries of at most 128 characters.

hostname.description:
Host name (RFC 1123): 1 to 253 characters, dot-separated labels of letters and
digits with hyphens only inside a label.

items.description:
Host profile: text values of at most 256 characters; `ips_private` and `ips_public`
are lists of up to 32 addresses.

Valid UTF-8, refused here before a use is taken: a JSON body always is, a query
string or a form body need not be, and the tags are echoed back after the commit.

Same body and rules as `POST /v1/tags`, but an existing key/value pair is not an error: that
tag is returned unchanged with 200.

ExtendMaintenanceRequest.description:
Gives a running or already completed maintenance more time. The window and the status
change in one step; the status follows from the new window.

message.description:
The timeline entry's text. Omit it and an automatic line is written in every
locale the organization publishes in.

scheduled_end.description:
Required as a KEY, nullable as a value: null means "open end, close it yourself".
Left optional, a forgotten field would quietly mean the same thing.

scheduled_start.description:
Moving the start too covers "not tonight after all" — a start in the future puts
the window back to `scheduled`.

ExtendMaintenanceRequest.title: ExtendMaintenanceRequest

ExtendRecurringWindowRequest.description: Which running window to extend, and its new end.

ends_at.description:
The new end (ISO 8601), on a full minute and in the future. At most seven days
after the window's regular start, and a short gap before the next window starts.

window_start.description:
The regular start of the running window (UTC, ISO 8601), as `window_start` of that
window in GET …/windows or GET /v1/maintenance-windows. It names the window you
mean: if another window is running by the time the request arrives, it is refused
with 409.

ExtendRecurringWindowRequest.title: ExtendRecurringWindowRequest

counts.description: How many heartbeats of the list were created, updated and left unchanged.

heartbeats.description:
Every heartbeat of the list that exists now, in the order of the list, in the
shape it was declared in. `result` is `created`, `updated` (the declaration changed
and the heartbeat was brought in line) or `unchanged`. `schedule`, `grace_seconds`,
`schedule_tolerance` and `max_duration_seconds` are what is in effect, which can
differ from what was sent: a period below the plan's shortest is raised, and
fields left out keep their value. `ping_url` is where the job reports to; treat
it like a password. `status` is `unknown` until the first ping arrives, then `up`
or `down`.

not_created.description:
The keys of the list that were not created. New heartbeats are created together
or not at all, so this is either empty or every new key. `reason` says why:
`service_limit` (the plan has no room for all of them; `missing` is how many
places are short), `creation_rate` (too many services created in the last hour or
day; `retry_after` is the number of seconds until there is room again, null when
the list is larger than one hour or day allows at all) or `blocked` (creating
services is switched off for the organization). Existing heartbeats are updated
either way.

skipped_tags.description:
Tags that could not be attached to the declared heartbeats because the
organization has no room for more tags. The heartbeats exist either way.

unlisted.description:
Heartbeats declared earlier for the same `app` and `environment` that the list did
not name, by key. Nothing was changed about them: they keep expecting pings until
you delete them.

HttpAuth.description: HTTP authentication. An update replaces the whole `auth` object, so send `type` and every field again.

password.description: Required when type=basic. Secret: responses show `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` instead. Send `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` in an update to keep the stored value.

token.description: Bearer token. Required when type=bearer. Secret: responses show `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` instead. Send `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` in an update to keep the stored value.

value.description: Header value. Required when type=api_key. Secret: responses show `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` instead. Send `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` in an update to keep the stored value.

HttpAuth.title: HttpAuth

conditions.description: Status rules evaluated against each check result. The fields and operators valid for this check type are listed at GET /v1/meta/check-types.

follow_redirects.description: Follow HTTP redirects (3xx). Disable to check the initial response only.

headers.description: Optional HTTP headers to send with the request. The values are secret: responses show `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` instead. An update replaces all entries, so send every entry you want to keep, with `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__` as the value to keep its stored value.

ip_version.description: Auto tries both IPv4 and IPv6 and reports "up" as soon as either is reachable. Choose ipv4 or ipv6 to force a single family (no fallback).

smart_dualstack.description: If the host offers both IPv4 and IPv6 but only one is reachable, report "Degraded" instead of "Up". Only applies when IP version is set to "auto".

verify_ssl.description: Verify the SSL certificate is valid. Disable for self-signed certificates.

ImageAppearance.description: Color scheme of the link preview image: `auto` (the default) lets the image follow the page, `light` and `dark` fix it.
ImageAppearance.title: ImageAppearance

kind.description:
`standard`, `agent_liveness` or `notice`. A notice is an announcement that concerns no
service: its `severity` is always `minor` and carries no meaning.

resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved (ISO 8601); null while it is open.

title.description: The incident title, localized to the request locale.

title_translations.description:
Every translation of the title as a `{locale: text}` map, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`;
null when the title has no translations.

updates.description: The public timeline updates of the incident. Internal notes are never included.

LogoSize.description: Logo height in the status page header: `small` (20 px), `medium` (28 px, the default) or `large` (40 px).
LogoSize.title: LogoSize

scheduled_end.description: null for an open-ended window ("until further notice") — ended manually only.

statuspages.description: The status pages that show this maintenance.

title.description: The maintenance title, localized to the request locale.

effect.description:
Recurring windows: `regular`, `moved` (an exception moved it) or `skipped` (an
exception lets it fall out). Always `regular` for a one-off maintenance.

ends_at.description: The end. Null for a one-off maintenance without a planned end.

id.description:
The window's own id. One-off: the maintenance id. Recurring: the recurring maintenance
id plus the regular start of the window in UTC; it stays the same when an exception
moves the window.

outcome.description:
Recurring windows that have a history entry: `running`, `completed`, `ended_early`,
`extended`, `skipped` or `missed`. Null otherwise.

service_ids.description:
The services this window covers (ids). Null for a coming recurring window: it covers
the services its recurring maintenance targets when it starts.

source_id.description: The id of the maintenance or recurring maintenance this window belongs to.

starts_at.description: Start of the window as planned (after exceptions for a recurring window).

state.description:
`scheduled`, `in_progress`, `completed` or `cancelled`. A recurring window counts as
in_progress only while it really runs; a skipped one is cancelled.

statuspage_ids.description: The status pages that show this window (ids). Empty: it is internal.

timezone.description: Recurring windows: the time zone the schedule is meant in. Null for a one-off one.

title_translations.description: The title in every language, keyed by language code.

window_start.description:
Recurring windows: the regular start of the window (UTC). Pass it as `window_start` to
end or extend this window. Null for a one-off maintenance.

MissingDataPolicy.description: What a condition does when a report lacks its metric (for example because the collector is off or a disk was removed). A missing value never counts as 0. `ignore` (default) skips the report and keeps the current state; `breach` counts it as over the threshold, which can cause false alarms; `recover` counts it as healthy.
MissingDataPolicy.title: MissingDataPolicy

deactivated_reason.description: Why the schedule was deactivated; null while it is active.

ends_at.description: When the schedule ends (ISO 8601); null for a schedule without an end.

OverrideEffect.description: What an exception does to the windows whose regular start lies in its period: `skip` leaves them out, `replace` holds the one window of the period at another time, starting inside the period.
OverrideEffect.title: OverrideEffect

PauseServiceRequest.description: Pauses a service, optionally until a point in time.

duration_minutes.description: How long the pause lasts, in minutes (1 to 129600 = 90 days).

note.description: Internal note for your team; never shown on a status page.

until.description:
When the service starts again by itself: ISO 8601 with offset, at least one minute
and at most 90 days ahead. Send this or duration_minutes, not both; neither pauses
until you resume it.

PauseServiceRequest.title: PauseServiceRequest

PreviewRecurrenceRequest.description: A rule to preview. Nothing is saved.

from.description: First instant of the preview (ISO 8601); default now.

maintenance_id.description:
Id of a recurring maintenance whose exceptions to apply, e.g. to see a rule change
together with the exceptions you already have.

schedule.description:
The rule to preview, same shape as on create. Unlike on create, a rule whose
windows overlap or lie only in the past is still previewed.

anchor_date.description:
First day the rule applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the maintenance's timezone. With an
interval above 1, the counting starts here.

duration_minutes.description:
Length of each window in minutes. Windows of one maintenance must not overlap and
need a short gap between them.

frequency.description: How often the window repeats: `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`.

interval.description:
Repeat every N days, weeks or months, e.g. 2 with `weekly` for every other week.
At least 1.

month.description: Monthly only: which day of the month.

day.description:
With mode `day`: 1 to 31, or `last` for the last day of the month. In a shorter
month (e.g. the 31st in April) the window falls on the month's last day.

mode.description:
`day` (a day of the month, see `day`) or `nth_weekday` (e.g. the second Tuesday,
see `nth` and `weekday`).

nth.description: With mode `nth_weekday`: 1 to 4, or `last` for the last such weekday of the month.

weekday.description: With mode `nth_weekday`: the weekday, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

start_time.description: Local start time of each window, `HH:MM`, 24-hour, e.g. `02:30`.

until_date.description:
Optional last day a window may start, `YYYY-MM-DD` (included). null or absent:
no end.

v.description: Version of the rule format. Always 1.

weekdays.description:
Weekly only: the weekdays the window starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, e.g.
[1, 3] for Monday and Wednesday. At least one.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the rule is meant in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`.

to.description:
End of the preview (ISO 8601), after `from`. The preview stops at `to` or after
`windows` windows, whichever comes first, and covers at most one year.

windows.description: Number of windows that take place; skipped ones are listed in between.

PreviewRecurrenceRequest.title: PreviewRecurrenceRequest

all_day.description: true: the period is whole days (`start_date` to `end_date`); false: an exact period.

effect.description:
`skip` (the windows of the period do not take place) or `replace` (the one window of
the period takes place at replacement_starts_at to replacement_ends_at).

end_date.description: Last day of the period, included. Null unless all_day.

expired.description: The period is over: the exception can no longer be changed or removed.

id.description: The id of the exception. Send it as `override_id` to change the exception.

notify_subscribers.description: The subscribers of the status pages were told about this exception.

reason.description: Internal note, never shown on a status page.

replacement_ends_at.description: For `replace`: end of the new window. Null for `skip`.

replacement_starts_at.description: For `replace`: start of the new window. Null for `skip`.

start_date.description: First day of the period (YYYY-MM-DD in the maintenance's time zone). Null unless all_day.

starts_at.description: Start of the period (always set, also for whole days).

created_at.description: When the recurring maintenance was created.

description_translations.description: The description in every language, keyed by language code. Null without one.

id.description: The id of the recurring maintenance.

lock_version.description:
The version of this state. Send it back with a change to be refused (409) instead of
overwriting a change someone made in between.

next_end_at.description: End of the running window, or of the next one. Null when paused or ended. Read-only.

next_start_at.description: Start of the running window, or of the next one. Null when paused or ended. Read-only.

notify_end.description: Subscribers of the status pages are notified when a window ends.

notify_start.description: Subscribers of the status pages are notified when a window starts.

paused.description: Paused by hand. A pause because of the plan limit is not shown here, see paused_reason.

paused_reason.description:
Why it is paused: `manual`, `plan_limit` (more recurring maintenances than your plan
allows; upgrade, then resume) or `org_deleted`. Null when not paused. Read-only.

rule_text.description:
The rule in plain words, in the same language as `title`, e.g. "Weekly on Sunday from
             * 02:00 to 03:00 (Europe/Berlin)". For display only; read the rule from `schedule`.

schedule.description:
The rule exactly as sent: `v`, `frequency`, `interval`, `weekdays` (weekly), `month`
(monthly), `anchor_date`, `start_time`, `duration_minutes` and `until_date` if set.

state.description:
`idle` (waiting for the next window), `running` (a window runs right now), `paused`
or `ended` (the rule has no further window). Read-only.

statuspage_ids.description: Status pages that show the maintenance (ids), sorted. Empty: it is internal.

tag_ids.description:
Tags (ids), sorted: every service carrying one of them when a window starts is
covered as well.

timezone.description: IANA timezone the rule is meant in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`.

title.description:
The title in one language: the one asked for with Accept-Language if the title has
it, otherwise your organization's default language.

title_translations.description: The title in every language, keyed by language code.

window_id.description: The id of that window, as listed by GET /v1/maintenance-windows.

window_start.description:
Regular start of that window (it differs from next_start_at when an exception moved
it). Pass it as `window_start` to end-window and extend-window.

ended_at.description: When it really ended; null while it runs and for a skipped or missed window.

planned_end_at.description: Planned end of the window, after exceptions.

planned_start_at.description:
Planned start of the window, after exceptions (differs from window_start when an
exception moved it).

service_ids.description: The services the window covered when it started (ids). Empty for a skipped or missed one.

started_at.description: When the window really started; null for a skipped or missed window.

window_start.description: Regular start of the window by the rule.

ResolveIncidentRequest.description: Resolves an incident. The message is posted as the final "resolved" timeline entry.

message.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

resolved_at.description:
When the service actually recovered. Defaults to now; a late close states the
real time so MTTR and the SLA window do not bill the reporting delay.

ResolveIncidentRequest.title: ResolveIncidentRequest

RotateAgentTokenRequest.description:
Replace the agent's token with a new one. The agent proves it is the registered instance by
sending its `instance_id`, so a leaked token alone cannot rotate.
RotateAgentTokenRequest.title: RotateAgentTokenRequest

RotationType.description: How a schedule rotates through its participants. With `manual`, no shifts are generated: you add them yourself.
RotationType.title: RotationType

SaveRecurringOverrideRequest.description: An exception to add, or to change (`override_id`).

all_day.description:
true: the period is whole days in the maintenance's timezone (`start_date` to
`end_date`). false or absent: an exact period (`starts_at` to `ends_at`).

effect.description:
`skip`: the windows whose regular start lies in the period do not take place.
`replace`: the one window whose regular start lies in the period takes place at
another time (`replacement_starts_at` to `replacement_ends_at`).

end_date.description:
With `all_day`: last day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, included. Not before
`start_date`.

ends_at.description: Without `all_day`: end of the period (ISO 8601), after `starts_at`.

lock_version.description:
The version of the maintenance you read (`lock_version`). If someone changed it
since, the request is refused with 409 instead of overwriting their change.
Optional.

notify_subscribers.description:
Tell the subscribers of the status pages about this change. Only when the
maintenance has `notify_start` or `notify_end` switched on. Default false.

override_id.description:
Id of an existing exception of this maintenance to change instead of adding a new
one.

reason.description: Internal note, never shown on a status page.

replacement_ends_at.description: For `replace`: end of the new window (ISO 8601), after `replacement_starts_at`.

replacement_starts_at.description:
For `replace`: start of the new window (ISO 8601), on a full minute, inside the
period.

start_date.description:
With `all_day`: first day of the period, `YYYY-MM-DD`, in the maintenance's
timezone.

SaveRecurringOverrideRequest.title: SaveRecurringOverrideRequest

enrollment_key_id.description:
The enrollment key the server enrolled with; null for older servers and once the key
has been deleted.

instance_conflict_at.description: Set when a second host reported with this agent's identity (a cloned machine).

observed.description:
The address LIVCK sees the agent call from, per IP family. Behind NAT this is the
network's address, not the host's.

private.description: Addresses the host reports for itself, at enrollment.

last_seen_at.description: When the agent last reported (ISO 8601); null before its first report.

os.description: Host facts the agent reports; null until it has.

reboot_required.description: True when the operating system asks for a reboot (pending updates).

state.description:
`waiting` until the first report, then `online`, `degraded`, `rebooting`, `updating`,
`offline`, `stopped`, `archived` or `uninstalled`.

available_version.description: The version the agent is meant to move to; null when it runs it already.

window_start.description: The host-local window (HH:MM) automatic updates run in.

ServiceCondition.description: A status rule applied to a check result. The valid `field` and `operator` combinations depend on the check type (and subtype, e.g. DNS record type) — fetch the matrix from GET /v1/meta/check-types.

field.description: Result field to assert, e.g. status_code, response_time_ms, json.data.status or header.content-type.

value.description: Comparison value; its JSON type depends on the field (number, string, boolean or array).

ServiceCondition.title: ServiceCondition

ServiceConfig.description: Check-type-specific monitoring configuration. The valid shape is determined by the service `check_type`; fetch the live field catalog from `GET /v1/meta/check-types`.
ServiceConfig.title: ServiceConfig

domain_alarm.description: Only on a domain alarm (`kind` = `domain`): what the alarm found for this service's domain.

added_at.description: When this service's domain joined the alarm (ISO 8601).

cleared_at.description: When no alarm rule fired any more for this domain (ISO 8601); null while it still does.

hits.description: The rules that fired, each with its key, level, and the value before and after.

kind.description:
`standard`, `agent_liveness` or `notice`. A notice is an announcement that concerns no
service: its `severity` is always `minor` and carries no meaning.

resolved_at.description: When the incident was resolved (ISO 8601); null while it is open.

service_impact.description: What this incident meant for the service you listed it through. Absent on a domain alarm.

added_at.description: When the service became part of the incident (ISO 8601).

impact.description: How badly the service was affected: `degraded`, `partial_outage` or `major_outage`.

is_recovered.description: Whether the service has recovered. A service can recover before the incident is resolved.

recovered_at.description: When the service recovered (ISO 8601); null while it is still affected.

title.description: The incident title, localized to the request locale.

title_translations.description:
Every translation of the title as a `{locale: text}` map, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`;
null when the title has no translations.

updates.description: The public timeline updates of the incident. Internal notes are never included.

anyOf.description:
The server behind an `agent` service: state, host facts, update settings. Null for
every other check type. Current figures: GET /v1/services/{id}/agent-metrics.

avg_response_ms.description:
Average response time over the last 30 days in milliseconds; null when nothing
was measured.

configured_at.description:
When monitoring was set up (ISO 8601). Null for an `http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `icmp`
or `ssl` service created without `settings`: it exists but is not checked until
you send `settings`.

domain_monitoring.description:
Domain monitoring: registration, zone and name servers of the target's domain. For
`http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `icmp` and `ssl` the checkbox `enabled` with its `rules`, for
`domain` its `rules` (`enabled` is always true). `rules` null = the default rules.
Read-only: `domain` (the registrable domain watched), `class` (`monitorable`, or why
the target cannot be watched: `ip`, `internal`, `private_suffix`, `unknown_tld`,
`invalid`) and `watch_id` (its facts: `GET /v1/domains/{watch_id}`), null until the
target has been looked at. Null for every other check type. Only present while
domain monitoring is available.

escalation_policy.description:
The escalation policy that alerts your team when this service fails. `source` says
where the assignment comes from: `manual` (set on the service) or `tag` (a policy
rule for one of the service's tags, named in `tag`). Null when no policy applies.

tag.description: The tag that assigns the policy (e.g. `env:prod`); null for `manual`.

favicon_url.description: Favicon of the monitored site, served from LIVCK's storage; null when none was found.

heartbeat.description:
The schedule of a `heartbeat` service and when it last pinged. Null for every other
check type. `schedule` has the shape of the answer to `POST /v1/heartbeats/declare`:
`period_seconds` for `simple`, `expression` for `cron`, the other one null.
`last_ping_at` is null until the first ping. `declared` is set when the heartbeat
was declared from the code of an application: `app`, `environment` and `key` name
it, `kind` is `schedule`, `job`, `queue` or `custom`. Null for a heartbeat created
by hand. The ping URL is never part of this resource.

last_check_at.description: When the latest check result arrived (ISO 8601); null before the first check.

maintenance.description:
Only on GET /v1/services/{id}: the maintenance window that runs on this service now,
else the next one within a year; null when there is none. `kind` is `one_time` or
`recurring`, `source_id` the maintenance it belongs to, `id` the window (as in
GET /v1/maintenance-windows), `window_start` the regular start of a recurring window.

paused_note.description: Internal note on the pause for your team; never shown on a status page.

paused_reason.description:
Why the service is paused: `manual`, `plan_limit`, `agent_limit`,
`agent_uninstalled` or `org_deleted`. Null while it is not paused.

paused_until.description:
When a paused service starts again by itself (ISO 8601); null when it stays paused
until it is resumed.

resume_failed_at.description:
When the service last failed to start again after a timed pause (ISO 8601). It then
stays paused; null once it is resumed or paused again.

resume_failed_reason.description:
Why it could not start again: `plan_limit`, `rate_limited`, `org_suspended` or
`error`. Null when resume_failed_at is null.

config.description: The check configuration, defaults included. Secret values (header values and the secrets under `auth`) are never returned: they read back as `__LIVCK_KEEP_UNCHANGED__`, and sending that value in an update keeps the stored secret.

probe_roles.description:
Role per monitoring location. `null` = the organization's roles apply; a
location absent from the map counts fully (`full`).

status.description: The raw monitored status. See effective_status for the override-aware value.

status_override_at.description:
Since when the status override applies (ISO 8601); null without an override. For an
override set by a maintenance window this is the planned start of the window, as long
as the override was written at most two minutes after it. Otherwise it is the moment
the override was set: a manual override, a window that was started early or late, or
a service added while the window was running.

status_override_source.description:
Who set the override: `manual` (a person, API or MCP), `maintenance` (a running
one-off maintenance) or `recurring` (a running window of a recurring maintenance).
A window removes its override again when it ends. Null without an override.

status_override_until.description:
When the status override ends by itself (ISO 8601): the end given to a manual
override, or the planned end of a recurring maintenance window. Null when it lasts
until it is removed, or without an override.

source.description:
`user` for tags you set, `system` for tags LIVCK maintains: the ones the server
agent sets (operating system, architecture, distribution) and the `livck.`
tags of heartbeats declared from code (`livck.app`, `livck.env`). System
tags cannot be removed by hand.

uptime_30d.description: Uptime over the last 30 days in percent (0–100); null when no data is available.

conditions.description: Status rules evaluated against each check result. The fields and operators valid for this check type are listed at GET /v1/meta/check-types.

ip_version.description: Auto tries both IPv4 and IPv6 and reports "up" as soon as either is reachable. Choose ipv4 or ipv6 to force a single family (no fallback).

smart_dualstack.description: If the host offers both IPv4 and IPv6 but only one is reachable, report "Degraded" instead of "Up". Only applies when IP version is set to "auto".

StatuspageAppearance.description: Light or dark mode of the public status page: `system` (the default) follows each visitor's device setting, `light` and `dark` open the page in that mode.
StatuspageAppearance.title: StatuspageAppearance

anyOf.description:
The status visitors see on the public page, derived live from an active
maintenance, an open published incident or the linked service (for a group: from
its visible children), whereas `status` is a stored value the page does not show.
Null when the component is not on the page (hidden, or inside a hidden group).

is_sync_managed.description:
True for components a tag-synced group added on its own. Their service and parent
cannot be changed and they cannot be deleted: remove the tag from the service instead.

allow_appearance_switch.description:
Whether visitors can switch between light, dark and system on the page. With `false`
everyone sees `appearance` and the switch is hidden.

appearance.description:
Light or dark mode of the public page: `system` follows each visitor's device
setting, `light` and `dark` open the page in that mode.

components.description: The page's components, in the same shape as `GET /statuspages/{id}/components`.

has_password.description: Whether a password is set. The password itself is never returned.

seo.description:
Search engine and link preview settings, with every default filled in. `title`,
`description` and `image_subtitle` are `{locale: text}` objects, `{}` when not set.
A text in a language the page no longer offers stays stored and applies again when
the language returns; it may be sent back unchanged.

supported_locales.description:
Languages set for this page. `null` means the page uses your organization's
languages. The `effective_*` fields show the languages the page actually serves.

url.description:
The address of the public page: `https://` plus its custom domain once that domain
is verified (`status: active`), otherwise `https://{slug}.statuspage.de`. With
several custom domains, the one attached first counts. An unpublished page returns
its URL too; the address answers with 404 until you publish the page.

StoreAgentConditionRequest.description:
A threshold condition on a metric the server agent reports. It fires when the value stays
past `threshold` for `duration_seconds` and then reports its `severity`.
StoreAgentConditionRequest.title: StoreAgentConditionRequest

StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest.description:
Creates an enrollment key: the credential the install command gives a server so it enrolls with
your organization. The key is in the response, once.

agent_tags.description:
Whether a server may add tags of its own at install (`--tag`). They only ever add to
the key's tags. True by default; a reseller organization cannot set it.

expires_at.description:
When the key stops working. `single`: 24 hours by default, at most 7 days. `fleet`:
90 days by default, at most 365 days.

max_uses.description:
`fleet` only: how many servers may enroll, 1 to 10000 (50 by default). A `single` key
always enrolls exactly one.

name.description: Shown in the console and in the key list.

tags.description:
Tag ids (from GET /v1/tags) or tag names, in any mix, as for services. Every server
enrolled with this key gets them, and the server cannot replace them. A tag that
fills a synced status page group is fine: the server never shows on the page.

type.description:
`single` (the default) enrolls exactly one server. `fleet` enrolls up to `max_uses`
servers, for images, cloud-init or configuration management.

StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest.title: StoreEnrollmentKeyRequest

StoreIncidentRequest.description:
Creates an incident. `title` and `message` accept a plain string (stored in your
organization's default language) or an object with one text per language, e.g.
`{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

kind.description:
'standard' (an outage, the default) or 'notice' — a standing public advisory that
has a date, a timeline, updates, subscribers and component links, but never moves
the banner, colours a component, counts as downtime or pages anybody.

message.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

resolved_at.description:
When the incident ended. Only meaningful together with status=resolved
(a history import); ignored otherwise. Without it a backfilled incident
ends the moment it started and reports a duration of zero.

service_ids.description:
Affected services (public ids from GET /v1/services). Duplicates are ignored; an id
that is not one of your services is rejected.

sla_counts_as_downtime.description:
Count this incident as downtime in SLA reports. Incidents created through the
API count as SLA downtime only when this is `true`, so set it when you import a
past outage.

started_at.description: When the incident started. Must not be in the future.

statuspage_ids.description:
Status pages to publish the incident on (public ids from GET /v1/statuspages).
Duplicates are ignored; an id that is not one of your status pages is rejected.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

StoreIncidentRequest.title: StoreIncidentRequest

StoreMaintenanceRequest.description:
Schedules a maintenance window. The start may be now, so a deploy script can open a
window on the spot.

message.description:
Optional first announcement, as plain text or an object with one text per
language. Empty falls back to a generated text. Appears in the timeline.

notify_announcement.description:
Whether subscribers are notified when the window is created. Defaults to true;
send false for a window nobody should hear about.

scheduled_end.description:
Omit or send null for an open-ended window ("until further notice").
Open-ended windows are ended manually — auto_complete never fires.

service_ids.description:
Services under maintenance (public ids from GET /v1/services). Duplicates are
ignored; an id that is not one of your services is rejected.

statuspage_ids.description:
Status pages to announce the window on (public ids from GET /v1/statuspages).
Duplicates are ignored; an id that is not one of your status pages is rejected.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

type.description:
planned = announced window (SLA-excluded by default); emergency =
unannounced (counts against the SLA). Defaults to planned.

StoreMaintenanceRequest.title: StoreMaintenanceRequest

StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest.description:
Record an absence. `user` is required and names the member who is away. `type` and `note`
are only returned to tokens with the `oncall.manage` permission.
StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest.title: StoreOnCallAbsenceRequest

StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest.description:
Ask for cover for a future shift of the token's creator. `shift` is that shift's id.
`requested_from` asks one participant of the schedule; without it, every other participant
is asked.
StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest.title: StoreOnCallCoverRequestRequest

StoreOnCallOverrideRequest.description:
Put a member on duty for a period, overriding the rotation. `user` is the member's id;
`null` leaves the period uncovered on purpose.
StoreOnCallOverrideRequest.title: StoreOnCallOverrideRequest

StoreOnCallScheduleRequest.description: Create an on-call schedule. The fields and rules are the same as in the web app.
StoreOnCallScheduleRequest.title: StoreOnCallScheduleRequest

StoreOnCallShiftRequest.description: Add a shift by hand. Only schedules with `rotation_type: manual` accept this (422 otherwise).
StoreOnCallShiftRequest.title: StoreOnCallShiftRequest

StoreRecurringMaintenanceRequest.description:
A new recurring maintenance: title, time zone, rule and the services, tags and status pages it
covers.

description.description: Optional description per language, same shape as `title`.

notify_end.description: Notify the subscribers of the status pages when a window ends. Default false.

notify_start.description: Notify the subscribers of the status pages when a window starts. Default false.

paused.description: Create it paused by hand: no window starts until you resume it. Default false.

schedule.description:
When the windows take place. Example for every Sunday 02:00 to 03:00:
{"v": 1, "frequency": "weekly", "interval": 1, "weekdays": [0],
"anchor_date": "2026-12-06", "start_time": "02:00", "duration_minutes": 60}.
The rule must produce at least one future window.

anchor_date.description:
First day the rule applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the maintenance's timezone. With an
interval above 1, the counting starts here.

duration_minutes.description:
Length of each window in minutes. Windows of one maintenance must not overlap and
need a short gap between them.

frequency.description: How often the window repeats: `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`.

interval.description:
Repeat every N days, weeks or months, e.g. 2 with `weekly` for every other week.
At least 1.

month.description: Monthly only: which day of the month.

day.description:
With mode `day`: 1 to 31, or `last` for the last day of the month. In a shorter
month (e.g. the 31st in April) the window falls on the month's last day.

mode.description:
`day` (a day of the month, see `day`) or `nth_weekday` (e.g. the second Tuesday,
see `nth` and `weekday`).

nth.description: With mode `nth_weekday`: 1 to 4, or `last` for the last such weekday of the month.

weekday.description: With mode `nth_weekday`: the weekday, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday.

start_time.description: Local start time of each window, `HH:MM`, 24-hour, e.g. `02:30`.

until_date.description:
Optional last day a window may start, `YYYY-MM-DD` (included). null or absent:
no end.

v.description: Version of the rule format. Always 1.

weekdays.description:
Weekly only: the weekdays the window starts on, 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday, e.g.
[1, 3] for Monday and Wednesday. At least one.

service_ids.description: Services every window covers (ids from GET /v1/services).

statuspage_ids.description:
Status pages that show the maintenance (ids from GET /v1/statuspages). Without any
it stays internal.

tag_ids.description:
Tags (ids from GET /v1/tags): every service carrying one of them when a window
starts is covered as well.

timezone.description:
IANA timezone the rule is meant in, e.g. `Europe/Berlin`. Windows keep their local
start time across daylight saving changes.

title.description:
Title per language, keyed by language code, e.g. {"de": "Nächtliches Backup",
"en": "Nightly backup"}. A plain string is taken as the title in the organization's
default language. Shown on the status pages and in notifications.

StoreRecurringMaintenanceRequest.title: StoreRecurringMaintenanceRequest

StoreServiceRequest.description:
Creates a service. With a `settings` block the service is fully configured and monitored
from this one request; without it the service is created but not monitored until it is
configured. Heartbeat and push monitors cannot be created through the API.

check_type.description:
One of the check types GET /v1/meta/check-types lists. `domain` only once domain
monitoring is available for everyone; until then it is refused with a message
that says so.

items.description: Must reference an active probe `code` from GET /v1/probes.

interval_seconds.description:
Seconds between checks, required whenever `settings` is sent. Your plan sets the
lowest allowed value (the minimum shown here is the lowest any plan allows); some
check types have their own bounds, see GET /v1/meta/check-types.

probe_roles.description:
Role per monitoring location, e.g. {"nyc": "reachability"}. A `reachability`
location still monitors and still triggers incidents — it is only excluded from
uptime/response-time metrics. Omitted locations are `full`; omit the whole map to
inherit the organization's roles.

tags.description:
Tag ids (from GET /v1/tags) or tag names, in any mix: `critical`, `key:value` or
`key=value` (the key is case-insensitive, the value exact). A name that does not exist
yet is created with the service. The exception is an entry that looks like a tag id
(21 letters, digits, `_` or `-`, with at least one uppercase letter): it is never
created and must be an existing tag's id or name.

StoreServiceRequest.title: StoreServiceRequest

StoreStatuspageComponentRequest.description:
Create a component. `parent_id` must be a group of the same page, and groups nest only a
limited number of levels deep (422 otherwise). `service_id` links a monitored service.

default_open.description:
Whether a group starts expanded on the public page (default true). A group with
an outage always opens, so this never hides a failure.

description.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 500
characters per language.

hide_operational_children.description:
Group option: hide children that are operational, so a healthy group shows as
a single row.

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

show_uptime_bars.description: Show uptime bars for this component on the public page.

sync_tag_id.description:
Makes the group tag-synced: it gets one child per service that carries this tag,
including services tagged later. You cannot change the service or parent of
these children or delete them; remove the tag from the service instead.

StoreStatuspageComponentRequest.title: StoreStatuspageComponentRequest

StoreStatuspageMetricRequest.description:
Create a metric chart. It shows on its own on the page, or under a component of the same
page when you set `component_id` (422 for a component of another page). Add its data with
the series endpoint.

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

suffix.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 10
characters per language.

StoreStatuspageMetricRequest.title: StoreStatuspageMetricRequest

name.description:
A plain string (stored in your organization's default language) or a `{locale: value}`
object such as `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}` that includes the default language. Max 255
characters per language.

StoreStatuspageRequest.title: StoreStatuspageRequest

StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest.description:
Add a series to a chart: one metric of a monitored service, e.g. `response_time_avg`. The
metric must exist for the service's check type (an ICMP service has no TLS timing),
otherwise 422.
StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest.title: StoreStatuspageSeriesRequest

StoreTagRequest.description:
Create a tag. A key/value pair that already exists is rejected with 422. When an existing
tag is fine, use `POST /v1/tags/ensure` with the same body.

value.description:
Optional. Free text (max 100 characters, no control characters); surrounding
whitespace is trimmed. Omit it, or send `null` or an empty string, for a tag
that is just a key.

StoreTagRequest.title: StoreTagRequest

source.description:
`user` for tags you created, `system` for tags LIVCK maintains: the ones the server
agent sets (operating system, architecture, distribution) and the `livck.` tags of
heartbeats declared from code (`livck.app`, `livck.env`). System tags cannot be
renamed, removed or deleted by hand.

conditions.description: Status rules evaluated against each check result. The fields and operators valid for this check type are listed at GET /v1/meta/check-types.

ip_version.description: Auto tries both IPv4 and IPv6 and reports "up" as soon as either is reachable. Choose ipv4 or ipv6 to force a single family (no fallback).

smart_dualstack.description: If the host offers both IPv4 and IPv6 but only one is reachable, report "Degraded" instead of "Up". Only applies when IP version is set to "auto".

UpdateAgentConditionRequest.description: Update a threshold condition; send only the fields you want to change.
UpdateAgentConditionRequest.title: UpdateAgentConditionRequest

UpdateIncidentRequest.description:
Changes incident properties. To add a timeline entry, or to change the status together
with a message, use `POST /v1/incidents/{incident}/updates`.

is_published.description: Not accepted on a domain alarm: that kind is never public.

notify_subscribers.description:
Only read when `is_published` turns an internal incident public: `false` publishes
it without notifying subscribers. Default `true`.

resolved_at.description:
Corrects the end time of an already resolved incident, e.g. an import that
landed with a duration of zero. Cannot be cleared.

severity.description: Not accepted on a notice (it has none) or a domain alarm (always `major`).

status.description:
New status. `resolved` is not accepted here: resolve an incident with
POST /incidents/{id}/resolve or by posting an update with status `resolved`.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

UpdateIncidentRequest.title: UpdateIncidentRequest

UpdateMaintenanceRequest.description:
Changes maintenance properties. Use the dedicated endpoints to start, complete or cancel
a maintenance: setting `status` here only changes the stored value, the affected services
are not switched into or out of maintenance.

post_update.description:
Rescheduling (a changed window) posts an auto timeline entry unless you opt out,
and only notifies subscribers when you explicitly ask for it.

scheduled_end.description:
Send null to clear the end → open-ended window ("until further notice"),
ended manually only (auto_complete cannot fire without an end).

service_ids.description:
Replaces the services under maintenance (public ids from GET /v1/services).
Duplicates are ignored; an id that is not one of your services is rejected.

statuspage_ids.description:
Replaces the status pages the window is announced on. Duplicates are ignored; an
id that is not one of your status pages is rejected.

title.description:
Plain text (stored in your default language) or an object with one text per
language, e.g. `{"de": "…", "en": "…"}`.

UpdateMaintenanceRequest.title: UpdateMaintenanceRequest

UpdateOnCallScheduleRequest.description:
Update an on-call schedule; send only the fields you want to change. Changing `starts_at`
does not shift the rotation. The shift preview accepts the same fields.
UpdateOnCallScheduleRequest.title: UpdateOnCallScheduleRequest

UpdateRecurringMaintenanceRequest.description: Changes to a recurring maintenance. Every field is optional; only the fields sent change.

description.description: Description per language, same shape as `title`. Replaces it; null removes it.

lock_version.description:
The version you read (`lock_version` of the maintenance). If someone changed the
maintenance since, the request is refused with 409 instead of overwriting their
change. Optional.

notify_end.description: Notify the subscribers of the status pages when a window ends.

notify_start.description: Notify the subscribers of the status pages when a window starts.

paused.description:
true pauses it by hand (a running window ends now), false resumes a maintenance you
paused. A pause caused by the plan limit is not shown here and not lifted here.

schedule.description:
The whole rule, replacing the current one (same shape as on create). Windows that
already ran stay in the history.

anchor_date.description:
First day the rule applies, `YYYY-MM-DD` in the maintenance's timezone. With an
interval above 1, the counting starts here.

duration_minutes.description:
Length of each window in minutes. Windows of one maintenance must not overlap and
need a short gap between them.

frequency.description: How often the window repeats: `daily`, `weekly` or `monthly`.

interval.description:

info.description:
The LIVCK Cloud public REST API lets you manage your monitoring programmatically:
services, incidents, scheduled maintenances, status pages and metrics.

**Authentication.** Every request needs an organization API token sent as a Bearer token:
`Authorization: Bearer lvk_...`. Tokens are organization service-accounts; create and manage
them under *Settings > Organization > API Tokens*. The API is available on the **Team** plan
and above.

**Localization.** Translatable fields (incident/maintenance `title`, update `message`) accept
either a plain string (stored under your default locale) or a `{ "de": "...", "en": "..." }`
object for multilingual content (the default locale is required). Responses resolve these
fields to a single string; send an `Accept-Language` header to pick another supported locale.

**Rate limiting.** 120 requests per minute per token. Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`
and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`; exceeding the limit returns `429`.

**Idempotency.** Every customer-API `POST` except the asset upload accepts an optional `Idempotency-Key`
header (1–255 visible ASCII characters, e.g. a UUID; scoped to the token). Repeating a request
with the same key and the same payload within 24 hours returns the stored response with
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` instead of running the action again. `409` (with `Retry-After`)
while the first request is still running, `422` when the key is reused with a different
payload. Only `2xx` responses are stored — after an error the key is free again.

**Errors.** Failures return a JSON envelope: `{ "message": "...", "errors": { ... } }` (the
`errors` object is present for `422` validation failures). Error messages are always in
English. A `403` or `402` caused by a plan limit also carries `upsell.reason: "limit"` and
`upsell.key`; a feature your plan does not include answers `403` with
`upsell.reason: "feature"`. Some limits, such as the number of tags, are reported as a
`422` validation error instead.

post.description:
Send every heartbeat one application expects in one environment, named by the `key` your
code uses for it. LIVCK finds each one again by `app`, `environment` and `key`:

- A key it does not know is created. The heartbeat waits for its first ping before it
  can go down.
- A key whose declaration changed is updated. Fields you send are set, fields you leave
  out keep the value they have. The name is only set when the heartbeat is created.
- A key declared as before is left alone, so the call can be repeated on every deploy.

Nothing is deleted or paused: a heartbeat that is missing from the list keeps expecting
pings and is named under `unlisted`. Delete it yourself once its job is gone.

New heartbeats count as services. When the plan or the creation limit has no room for
all new ones, none of them is created (`not_created`), the existing ones are still
updated, and the call answers 200.

The token needs `heartbeats.declare` (a token that may create and edit services has it)
and must see the whole organization. A token whose view is limited by access areas is
refused with 403 and `code: restricted_view`.

Example:

```json
{
  "app": "shop",
  "environment": "production",
  "heartbeats": [
    {
      "key": "export:nightly",
      "kind": "schedule",
      "schedule": { "type": "cron", "expression": "0 3 * * *", "timezone": "Europe/Berlin" }
    },
    {
      "key": "queue:default",
      "kind": "queue",
      "schedule": { "type": "simple", "period_seconds": 60 }
    }
  ]
}
```

Pass `name`, `check_type` and (for non-`manual` types) `target`. The optional
`settings` block configures and immediately starts monitoring in one call.

`settings.config` and `settings.config.conditions` are **specific to the
check type** — fetch the live field/operator catalog from
`GET /v1/meta/check-types`, and valid `settings.assigned_probes` codes from
`GET /v1/probes`. Omit `assigned_probes` to inherit the organization's
default locations.

`settings.probe_roles` gives a location a role: `full` (default — counts for
outage detection AND for uptime/response-time metrics) or `reachability`
(still checks, still triggers incidents and alerts, but is excluded from the
metrics). At least one location must remain `full`. Omit the map to inherit
the organization's roles.

`domain_monitoring` watches the registration, zone and name servers of the
target's domain: for `http`, `tcp`, `dns`, `icmp` and `ssl` the checkbox
(`enabled`, on unless sent false) and its `rules`, for `domain` its `rules`.
Omit `rules` for the default rules. Until domain monitoring is available the
field is refused (422) and not shown.

Example (HTTP service with a custom header and a body condition):

```json
{
  "name": "API health",
  "check_type": "http",
  "target": "https://api.example.com/health",
  "settings": {
    "interval_seconds": 60,
    "timeout_seconds": 10,
    "retries": 2,
    "assigned_probes": ["ffm", "hel"],
    "config": {
      "method": "GET",
      "headers": { "X-Api-Key": "secret" },
      "conditions": [
        { "field": "status_code", "operator": "gte", "value": 400, "status": "down" },
        { "field": "response_time_ms", "operator": "gt", "value": 2000, "status": "degraded" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

The tag is removed from every service that carries it; the services stay.
Fails with 422 while the tag is still in use: by a tag-synced status page
group, an SLA objective, an access area or an escalation or incident
policy. System tags (`source: system`), set by the server agent or by a
heartbeat declaration, cannot be deleted.
